transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I just... well, I've been a little, I guess, overly productive lately? Which I know usually sounds like a good thing! But, um, I went from barely being able to unpack and settle into my new apartment to... just suddenly saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, and taking on extra client prototypes for work. I even started redesigning my entire design portfolio from scratch. 

It was like I just had to fix my whole life in one giant sprint, you know? Does that make sense as a reason to come in? I really hope I'm not wasting your time with this.

Can you tell me more about when this sudden increase in productivity started? Was there also a time when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt an intense rush of energy that lasted for several days or more?

Um, well, it started earlier this month, I think? And yes, I did have a lot of energy. It actually felt really great at first, like I was just... electric, you know? Just really upbeat and ready to tackle everything. I hope that doesn't sound too strange, being happy about having energy. 

But, um... I guess I did get a little... impatient? Which really isn't like me, I swear! I'm usually very easygoing. But I found myself snapping at one of my contractors, and even my sister, over just... tiny little delays. It felt like they were, I don't know, personally trying to block me from getting things done? I feel terrible about it now, I really do. I apologized to them, of course. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During this time of increased energy and productivity, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual, or were you able to go with much less sleep without feeling tired?

Um, well, yes, I guess my sleep did change a little bit. But honestly, it didn't feel like a problem at the time! I hope it's okay to say that. 

For, um, maybe several nights in a row, I was only sleeping about three or four hours. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all! I woke up feeling completely fine, like I was totally rested. I just thought, you know, maybe my body was just being super efficient? So I figured I should just use the extra time to get ahead on all my projects. I didn't want to waste the day lying in bed if I was already awake and ready to go. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right. I know it sounds a little strange now, but it really just felt like I was being productive.

During this time of increased energy and productivity, did you notice that your mood was consistently elevated, expansive, or unusually irritable in a way that felt distinctly different from your usual self?

Um, yes, I think so. Like I was saying before, it was just... it felt so different from how I normally am. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little bit. 

But earlier this month, I just had this... this feeling of being almost electric, you know? Just so upbeat and positive. But then, almost in the same breath, I'd get so frustrated. Like when I snapped at that contractor, and my sister. It was over such tiny, silly delays, but in the moment, it felt like they were doing it on purpose? Like they were personally trying to block me from getting all my work done. 

It was just... very out of character for me. I'm usually much more patient, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm normally that difficult to work with. Does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what happened.
Was there a specific period during this time when you felt like you didn’t need any sleep at all, or could function fully even with very little sleep?

Um, yes, I think we touched on this a little bit just a moment ago. I hope you don't mind me bringing it up again! 

But yes, there was definitely a stretch there... for several nights, I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours. And the funny thing is, I didn't feel like I was dragging at all. I woke up completely convinced I was totally fine, you know? Like my body just didn't need the rest. 

I just figured, well, if I'm awake and feeling this good, I should probably just use the extra time to get ahead on all my design projects. I didn't want to just lie there in the dark if I could be doing something useful. Does that sound like what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

Can you confirm if there was a clear period lasting at least one week where your mood was noticeably elevated, expansive, or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, along with this increased energy and productivity?

Um, well, yes, it was definitely longer than a week. I really hope I'm giving you the right timeline here, but... this whole intense up-and-down pattern? It's actually been going on since I moved into my new apartment, which was about a month ago now. 

So, um, yes, it's been nearly every day for the past month. I know a month sounds like a long time to be acting so... well, intense, and I feel a little embarrassed that I let it go on that long without realizing it might be an issue. I really just thought I was settling into the new place and getting a lot of design work done! 

Does that help answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.

During this time of increased energy and productivity, did you notice any other changes in your thinking or behavior, like feeling overly confident, talking more than usual, having racing thoughts, or taking on too many projects at once?

Um, well... I guess I did take on quite a bit. I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I was being completely reckless or anything, because I really was getting things done. But, um... yeah, I went from just barely trying to unpack boxes in my new apartment to suddenly... well, just saying yes to everything. 

I started volunteering for mentoring sessions, which I normally love, but I took on a lot of them. And I started doing all these extra client prototypes on top of my normal workload. Oh, and I decided I needed to completely redesign my entire portfolio right then and there. It was like... like I felt this sudden pressure that I had to fix my entire career and life in one giant sprint, you know? 

I know it sounds like I bit off way more than I could chew, and I probably did. I just... I wanted to be helpful and productive. Is it okay that I took on that much? I mean, does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right examples.
During this time, did you notice that your thoughts were racing, or that it was hard to slow your mind down, like one idea quickly led to another?

Um, I wouldn't really say my thoughts were racing, exactly. I hope that's the right way to describe it. I mean, I definitely had a lot of ideas, especially with the portfolio redesign and all the new prototypes, but it didn't feel... out of control, you know? 

It felt more like I was just really inspired and making good connections between different design concepts. I don't think it was hard to slow down, I just didn't really want to because I was on such a good roll. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you mean by racing thoughts. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how my mind was working.

Can you confirm that during this time, there was a distinct period lasting at least one week where your mood was clearly different from your usual self—either unusually high, overly confident, or easily irritated, even if others didn’t notice it at the time?

Um... yes, I suppose my mood was definitely different from my usual self. I really hope I don't sound awful admitting this, because I always try to be very professional and easy to get along with, but... earlier this month, I felt almost... electric, I guess? Like, incredibly upbeat one minute. 

But then... well, I actually snapped at a contractor I work with, and even my sister. It was over such tiny delays, but in the moment, it felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting my work done. I feel so embarrassed about getting irritated with them like that... I really usually never act that way, and I've been kicking myself for it. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for several days or longer?

Um... yes. Actually, that's... that's kind of why I'm here. I hope it's okay to talk about this part, because it's... it's really hard to admit. I always try to be a positive person, you know? But... lately... 

Well, lately I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling right in my chest. And it's so silly, because my apartment will be perfectly quiet, nothing bad is happening at all, and I'll just look at a coffee mug sitting in the sink and feel like I could just break down and cry over it. 

I know that sounds ridiculous, crying over a mug. I'm usually so much more put together than that. I just... I feel so down, and I don't even have a good reason for it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean by feeling down or hopeless? I really hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy, almost every day?

Um... yes, definitely longer than two weeks. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I know people go through hard times, but... these heavier stretches, where I just feel so low... they've actually been happening on and off for a while. 

I guess they started showing up around 11 months ago, right after my separation. I tried so hard to just push through it and be strong, you know? But then I had this recent move, and it just seemed to make all those heavy feelings so much sharper and harder to ignore. 

I feel bad complaining about it, because I know I should be able to handle a move and a breakup like a normal adult. But it's just been really lingering. Does that make sense? I hope that's the right timeline you were looking for.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Bipolar II Disorder, characterized by at least one current or recent hypomanic episode and one prior major depressive episode. The hypomanic episode includes elevated mood, increased goal-directed activity, reduced need for sleep, and irritability, lasting for at least one week. The major depressive episode includes persistent low mood, anhedonia, and emotional dysregulation over a period exceeding two weeks.
